I just got an Oxy-Acetylene rig, and I'm just learning how to weld. I found this sub and got really excited... then I got sad.

Anyone still around?
Ask away ! Seasoned shop fabricator here rdy to help

Is there any reason people stopped using Acetylene for small welding jobs? I'm a hobby blacksmith and was just looking for something to make small welds on pieces that are too awkwardly shaped to easily forgeweld. So far, I'm really enjoying learning. I can't understand why people dropped the gas welding models.

Good question...

There are lots of reasons, from a purely business standpoint :

  • Tig welding is much more efficient & economical. Setting up is quicker, you have an instant puddle, amazing heat control, faster weld speeds are easily achievable, a wide range of bastard alloys & exotic metals can be tig welded and post weld cleaning is often unecessary. Not as many safety issues either.

  • OAW stations can easily be dangerous if not well maintained, tips are easily damaged and copper is getting expensive, so is acetylene. Modern trade schools don't teach it much if at all, only cutting, so good gas welders are very rare nowadays.

Even though I do mostly Tig, I love getting the odd cast iron brazing job. Kicking it old school is the best gift my boss can give me... too bad it's a dying art.

So watcha smithering on these days ?

Lately I've been making some rail-spike knives for friends, gotta get those commissions... I've just moved into a fixer-upper from the early 1900s and my wife and I decided on an industrial theme, so I'm working on designing some decorative pieces like coat hooks, kitchen hangers, some grating, etc. The grating is where I'm thinking the welding will come in most handy. There are some pieces that I would just feel more comfortable making in smaller chunks and welding together than trying to forge weld them and manipulate the giant things, even if they will end up a reasonable size.
